title: Genki Manta: The Controller That Thinks It's a Console
summary: The Genki Manta, unveiled at Gamescom, transcends traditional gamepads by integrating a display, a full operating system, and a Raspberry Pi chip. This innovative device offers unparalleled configuration options and even allows for playing simple games directly on the controller itself.
content:
In a world teeming with incremental updates, a new contender has emerged at Gamescom that challenges the very definition of a game controller. The Genki Manta, initially appearing somewhat bulky in photographs, melts into the hands with surprising ergonomic grace, offering a comfortable and secure grip from the first touch.

But what truly sets it apart isn't just its tactile feel; it's the audacious technology packed within. Beyond modern TMR joysticks, celebrated for their superior precision and customizable resistance—a boon for eliminating stick drift and tailoring input—the Manta houses its own full-fledged display. This isn't merely for aesthetics; it’s the window into a proprietary operating system, powered by a dedicated Raspberry Pi chip, turning the Manta into something far more intelligent than your average gamepad.

This integrated OS transforms the controller into a highly versatile device. While it can even run small, standalone games directly on its display, the true genius lies in its deep, intuitive configuration capabilities. Gamers can fine-tune every aspect of their experience, from button mapping and macro creation to adjusting joystick sensitivity on the fly, all managed through the display. This level of comprehensive, on-device customization elevates the Genki Manta beyond a mere input device, positioning it as a powerful, personal gaming hub for the discerning enthusiast seeking ultimate control over their digital adventures.
keyTakeaways: The Genki Manta is a unique controller featuring an integrated display and its own operating system.
Powered by a Raspberry Pi chip, the controller offers advanced configuration options and can even run small games.
It boasts modern TMR joysticks for enhanced precision and customizable resistance, alongside impressive ergonomics despite its appearance.
author: Silvio Werner

title: OpenAI Just Pulled the Plug on Musk-Owned Cursor, Citing Trust and Contract Violations
summary: OpenAI has announced it will terminate its contract with Cursor, a coding AI startup recently acquired by Elon Musk's SpaceX. The move is a direct consequence of OpenAI's lack of trust in Musk's companies, specifically citing past contractual breaches by xAI and X (formerly Twitter).
content:
In a move that further sharpens the already frosty relationship between two titans of artificial intelligence, OpenAI has announced it will sever ties with Cursor, a coding AI startup recently brought under the wing of Elon Musk’s SpaceX. This contractual dissolution isn't merely a business formality; it's a direct jab, with OpenAI explicitly stating its decision stems from a lack of trust in Musk’s companies to adhere to its terms of service.

The core of OpenAI’s concern lies in what it describes as a pattern of non-compliance. While the immediate trigger is Cursor's acquisition by SpaceX, OpenAI pointed fingers directly at previous conduct by xAI, Musk’s own AI venture designed to compete with OpenAI, and even the platform X (formerly Twitter). The implication is clear: OpenAI believes entities under Musk's control have demonstrated a disregard for contractual obligations and ethical compliance in the past, making a continued partnership untenable.

This incident casts a spotlight on the complex and often contentious history between OpenAI and Elon Musk. A co-founder of OpenAI, Musk later departed to become a vocal critic, eventually launching xAI with the stated aim of building "truth-seeking AI." This latest action by OpenAI underscores the escalating rivalry, suggesting that the battle for AI dominance isn't just about technological superiority but also about trust, data governance, and adherence to foundational agreements.

For Cursor, a promising startup aimed at making developers more efficient with AI-powered coding, this breakup with a leading AI model provider could significantly impact its offerings and future trajectory. OpenAI's unwavering commitment to protecting its intellectual property and ensuring its ecosystem partners play by the rules sends a clear message across the competitive landscape: business relationships in the high-stakes world of AI are increasingly contingent on more than just technological prowess, demanding absolute adherence to agreements. The AI industry watches closely as this high-profile spat unfolds, signaling a new frontier in the battle for ethical and competitive dominance.
keyTakeaways: OpenAI is terminating its contract with Cursor, a coding AI startup recently acquired by Elon Musk's SpaceX.
The decision stems from OpenAI's explicit distrust in Musk's companies, citing past contractual breaches by xAI and X (formerly Twitter).
This move escalates the ongoing rivalry between OpenAI and Elon Musk's various tech ventures, emphasizing trust and compliance as critical factors in the AI industry.
author: Lloyd Lee,Truman Dickerson

title: Bitcoin Miners Unchained: Why Their Fortunes Are Diverging from BTC's Rally
summary: Bitcoin miners are increasingly decoupling from the cryptocurrency's price movements, as evidenced by recent market performance where most major mining stocks fell despite a significant BTC rally. This divergence signals a strategic shift as these companies pivot towards becoming high-performance computing (HPC) hubs, leveraging their infrastructure beyond mere crypto mining.
content:
The world of cryptocurrency mining is undergoing a profound transformation, challenging long-held assumptions about its direct correlation with Bitcoin's performance. Recent market data paints a stark picture: while Bitcoin surged an impressive 21.5% between August 17th and August 21st, a staggering six out of seven major US-listed mining companies saw their stock values drop, some significantly.

Only MARA Holdings managed to track Bitcoin closely with a 16.1% increase, but giants like Cipher Digital plummeted 14.8%, and TeraWulf shed 11.2%. This glaring disconnect isn't merely a blip; it's a testament to an evolving industry strategy. Miners are no longer content being pure crypto proxies, their valuations solely tied to the volatile whims of Bitcoin. Instead, they are aggressively re-branding and re-tooling.

The strategic pivot is clear: these operations are morphing into high-performance computing (HPC) powerhouses. Their massive investments in data center infrastructure, robust power grids, and advanced cooling systems, initially dedicated to solving complex cryptographic puzzles, are now being eyed for a far broader spectrum of compute-intensive tasks. Think artificial intelligence, machine learning, and vast data processing – industries with insatiable demands for computational muscle.

This shift allows miners to diversify their revenue streams, reducing their existential reliance on Bitcoin's price and network difficulty. By leasing out their formidable computing capabilities, they unlock new avenues for growth and stability, potentially transforming them into crucial players in the burgeoning digital infrastructure landscape. While still nascent, this strategic reorientation suggests a future where these companies are valued not just by the blocks they mine, but by the myriad computational services they provide.
keyTakeaways: Most US-listed Bitcoin miners recently saw their stock prices fall despite a significant Bitcoin rally, indicating a decoupling from BTC's direct price influence.
Bitcoin mining companies are strategically transitioning their business models to become high-performance computing (HPC) hubs.
This pivot allows miners to diversify revenue by leveraging their existing infrastructure for AI, machine learning, and other data processing needs, reducing reliance on Bitcoin's volatility.
author: Andjela Radmilac
